help.analysis_step.after: What follows approval depends on the work mode: if you do not want Maestro to write the code, say /mode-change human_lead — you keep the analysis and a human writes the code.
help.analysis_step.answer: Maestro posts its first comment within minutes. If information is missing it asks, and you answer in a comment — there is no form to fill. It is forbidden to invent what it does not know; it must ask.
help.analysis_step.decide: If you are happy write /approve. If something is missing write /reject <reason>; the agent fixes it in the same session rather than starting over.
help.analysis_step.open: Open an ordinary Jira ticket; free text is enough and no field is mandatory. If your project is in opt-in mode add the maestro label or comment /ai-start.
help.analysis_step.review: An "analysis ready" comment arrives: purpose, scope, impact matrix, acceptance criteria and risk. The template is the institution's own, managed from the analysis template designer in the Studio.
help.analysis_walkthrough: "I want an analysis" — step by step
help.command_desc.ai_assign: Assigns an unmatched ticket to an application.
help.command_desc.ai_explain: Explains the last change in plain language.
help.command_desc.ai_start: Starts the flow on a project in opt-in mode.
help.command_desc.ai_takeover: Hands work back from a human to the AI; the branch is rebased.
help.command_desc.approve: Approves the gate. The comment must contain nothing else; authority and separation of duties are checked automatically.
help.command_desc.mode_change: Changes the work mode: full_auto, ai_assist, human_lead or human_only.
help.command_desc.reject: Rejects; the reason is passed to the agent in the same session.
help.command_desc.status: Summarises which step the work is on.
help.knowledge: What does the AI work from?
help.knowledge_body: The model learns your institution from the Knowledge library; it is whatever you upload: the analysis template, two or three example past analyses, coding standards, repo cards and security/process documents — all versioned.
help.role_desc.admin: The Studio is your screen: connections, project binding, parameters and monitoring are managed here.
help.role_desc.business: You never leave Jira: you write the ticket and reply to the analysis comment with /approve or /reject <reason>. You do not need to open the Studio.
help.role_desc.developer: Jira and ADO are enough. You review the PR in ADO; with /mode-change you can take the work over and Maestro moves to observing.
help.safety_rails: Safety rails: it must ask what it does not know and may not invent; no analysis becomes code without human approval; the AI cannot touch protected_paths directories.
help.setup_step.app: The add-application wizard: bind the ADO repository, take the .maestro.yaml PR suggestion, then review and approve the AI's repo-card discovery.
help.setup_step.binding: Jira binding and matching: bind the project, then choose the trigger mode (automatic, label or command) and the matching rules.
help.setup_step.connections: Settings and connections: the Jira DC address and service account token, the ADO token, Vault and the LLM accounts. Secrets are written to Vault.
help.setup_step.dry_run: A dry run is mandatory: preview where the last 20 tickets would land, then activate if you are happy. Pausing or unbinding a project stays possible at any time.
help.setup_step.permissions: Service account permissions: Browse, Comment, Edit (label), Assign, Create/Link Issue. No workflow change, custom field or plugin is required — no Jira admin burden on the institution.
help.setup_step.webhook: Ask the Jira admin for a single global webhook, once (issue created/updated and comment). There is no per-project webhook or JQL to maintain; the filter lives inside Maestro.
help.summary: You write a ticket in Jira; Maestro reads it, asks in a comment if something is missing, and writes the analysis. You approve it; it writes the code in an isolated sandbox and really runs the tests, then opens a PR. A human approves the PR and it is merged. Nothing is released to production — release stays the institution's own process.
help.trouble.quota: If quota runs out the work does not fail; it waits in the queue and resumes when a window opens. You can follow it on the Cost and LLM Gateway screens.
help.trouble.rejected: If the analysis or code is not good, write /reject <reason>; this is the normal flow and the agent fixes it.
help.trouble.stuck: If the agent is stuck: after three rejections or three CI failures the work is handed to a human automatically and a notification goes out.
help.trouble.wrong_app: If a ticket landed on the wrong application, correct it with /ai-assign <application>.

runners.accepted_risk.body: Windows and macOS have no container isolation — Xcode and MSBuild do not fit in a container. Compensating controls: ephemeral user, least privilege, EDR and the same egress rules. This is recorded in the plan as an accepted risk.

runners.isolation.windows_macos.value: Ephemeral user and workspace per job · least privilege · MDM/EDR · audited cleanup afterwards

sandbox.note.no_delete: There is no delete button here: an idle workspace is archived on its own schedule (M65). A delete control in an operator's hand is the easiest way to destroy the session a human is working in — which is why "a human is working in it" is shown as its own state.
sandbox.note.no_transcript: This screen shows session state, not session output: a live agent transcript can contain unmasked ticket text (M18) and is not carried into the browser.

template.field.ai_instruction: Instruction to the AI — how should it fill this section?
template.field.ai_instruction_hint: This text goes into the agent's prompt.
template.field.description_hint: Shown under the heading in the Studio and in the document.
template.field.example_hint: Given to the agent as the measure of a good answer.
template.field.required_off_hint: Optional: if it is not relevant the agent may write "no change" and move on.
template.field.required_on_hint: If it is missing the analysis never reaches a human gate — the agent regenerates it (fail-closed).
template.field.title: Section title
template.format_hint.bullet_list: A bullet list is expected · schema: array of text (at least 3 items).
template.format_hint.free_text: A plain paragraph is expected · schema: text (at least 2 sentences).
template.format_hint.impact_matrix: A platform × module matrix is expected · schema: {platform, module, impact, sub-ticket} — fan-out sub-tickets are opened from this section.
template.format_hint.table: A table with headers is expected · schema: row objects — becomes a real table in the Word output.
template.last_section: A template must keep at least one section.
template.new_section_instruction: Tell the agent here how to fill this section.
template.no_example: — no example given; the agent works from the instruction alone
template.order_note: The order here is the section order in the document. Change it with ↑ ↓.
template.pick_section: Pick a section on the left, or add a new one.
template.pin_note: Version pinning (M83): every run finishes on the version it started with. Publishing a new version does not move open runs; the version used is recorded on the ticket and in the evidence package.
template.placeholder_is: Its placeholder in the Word output:
template.preview_hint: The structure validation runs against, shown with each section's own example text.
template.section_removed: Section removed — saving publishes this as a new version.

users.card.lookup_sub: What Maestro believes about a directory account
users.card.roles_sub: A closed set — a session's authority is read from this list
users.note.ai_cannot_approve: The AI service account cannot approve anything — it technically has no such permission.
users.note.directory_owns_roles: Roles are not granted in Maestro: identity and authority come from the directory's group membership (M8). This screen reads that mapping, it does not change it — which is why there is no role editor and no deactivate button here. Authority changes are made in the directory.
users.note.disabled_sessions: ⚠ This account is disabled. Disabling prevents new sign-ins, but **a token issued earlier can remain valid until it expires** (sessions are eight hours and do not slide). If access must be proven cut off, verify token revocation on the directory/session side.
users.note.role_not_in_force: This role is not in force because the account is disabled.
users.sod.ai_cannot_approve: The AI service account cannot approve

users.sod.qa_split: QA scenario approval ≠ QA result approval
